doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: Royalties through BMI and administrators
summary: Payments for use of his music come through BMI and a company such as Universal.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Well this is not a personal question but I guess I’m just curious, when you go to your mailbox everyday do you sometimes expect payments from these people or these companies that are using your music?

Oh yeah well what happens is well you know — I know you know — you have BMI and you’ve got ASCAP. So I’m with BMI. And so every time it’s played or performed on the TV or radio, you know, it’s recorded that there be, that’s when you look for things. Or you have a company like Universal Music or someone to administrate things, because it’s happening all over the world so you know I can’t check everything all over the world.
Well I’m glad it seems to be, that the protocols are in place that you’re being recognized and compensated for that.
